sentence: A 7-year-old girl with no relevant history was referred from her primary care center for presenting a lesion on the right cheek, somewhat itchy and painful, which had not improved after oral treatment with amoxicillin/clavulanic acid, prescribed practically from the beginning for two weeks. previous.
On examination, she showed an erythematous-violet nodule on her right cheek, cold and soft to the touch, well-defined, 1.5 cm in diameter.
No regional lymph nodes were palpable, although there was a slight keratosis pilaris on the skin of the cheeks.

Given the clinical suspicion of FATF, and the parents were informed about the benignity of the process, it was agreed with them not to perform a skin biopsy and to schedule periodic follow-up, along with therapy with metronidazole gel at night.
Two weeks later, spontaneous drainage of bloody-purulent material from the center of the lesion occurred, with subsequent progressive resolution of the nodule over the course of about 6 weeks.
Cultures for bacteria, fungi, and mycobacteria from the drainage exudate were negative.
However, after resolution of the nodular lesion, some residual telangiectasias persisted in the affected area, which have slowly attenuated during the 10 months of follow-up.

We advise the patient to undergo check-ups until the process is completely resolved and warn of the need to consult if symptoms or clinical signs suggestive of ocular rosacea appear (dryness or redness of the eyes, blepharitis, chalazion, photophobia, loss of visual acuity).
